chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra, from Umar ibn Hanzala who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is your view regarding a cup of an intoxicant upon which water is poured until its normality goes away and its intoxication goes away?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by Allah, and there is no drop which drops into a container except that container must be emptied'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an intoxicant if water is poured over it to remove its taste and effect?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'kathir' (abundant) intoxicants, where the presence of any measurable amount of intoxication renders the entire volume prohibited, regardless of dilution. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the ruling is intrinsic to the liquid's nature rather than its sensory properties, meaning that even if the taste and immediate effect are masked, the prohibition remains absolute. This serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between 'kathir' and 'qalil' (small amount) intoxicants, emphasizing that the latter does not necessarily render the whole substance impure.
